flooding is occurring, confirmed by local emergency management.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Upper Gila River Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Much of southwest New Mexico, including the Dona Ana,
Grant, Luna, Hidalgo, and Sierra Counties and the Sacramento
Mountain in south-central New Mexico.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT early this morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Abundant moisture has moved into the region and scattered to
numerous showers and thunderstorms will continue tonight. Many
areas west of the Rio Grande have received a half inch up to 2
inches of rainfall over recent days, so any additional rainfall
could lead to flash flooding. Localized storm amounts of 1 to 2
inches are still possible with the strongest storms and where
storms redevelop over the same area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Southwest Desert/Mimbres Basin; Eastern Black Range Foothills; Sierra County Lakes; Northern Dona Ana County; Southern Dona Ana County/Mesilla Valley; West Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500 Feet; Sacramento Mountains Above 7500 Feet; East Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500 Feet
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest New Mexico,
including Sierra, Dona Ana, Luna, and eastern Grant Counties and
the Sacramento Mountains in northern Otero County.

* WHEN...From Noon MDT today through 6 AM MDT Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, arroyos, low water crossings, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 24-hour rainfall observations shows a wide swath of 1-2" across
much of south-central New Mexico. High soil moisture will allow
runoff to occur quickly with any additional rounds of rain.
Thunderstorms are expected to track north across the Watch area
Thursday night into Friday morning, leading to localized flash
flooding. Additionally, risk of flooding continues for the
Sacramento Mountains, where storms initiating along a N/S
oriented ridge and parallel storm motions may lead to training
storms and prolonged heavy rain Thursday afternoon.
- This includes portions of the I-25 corridor through Hatch and
Truth-or-Consequences and the I-10 corridor through Las Cruces
and Deming.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Navajo, AZ
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is
imminent or occurring. Water flowing over roadways will create
slick roads and muddy unpaved roads. Ponding of water on
interstates, highways and in urban areas will create hazardous
travel conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 342 AM MST, ADOT street flooding on SR-260 is ongoing. Between
0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Show Low Creek and Hog Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Show Low and Linden.
- This includes State Route 260 between mile markers 334 and 336.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
